Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 6:36pm

Rory Lobb kicked two vital fourth quarter goals as the Western Bulldogs saw off the challenge from St Kilda at Docklands.

  (Getty Images: Quinn Rooney)

The Western Bulldogs get the points at Docklands against St Kilda to finish round 15, as the Saints lose two key players to injury.

Earlier North Melbourne saw off Richmond by 25 points at the MCG to sit inside the top 10.

Marcus Bontempelli kicked an incredible goal with a one-handed scoop, turn and kick, along with 34 disposals.

The Saints trailed for much of the game, but their chances were not helped by losing key defender Jack Sinclair in the first quarter to a calf injury, before ruckman Tom De Koning left the game with a rib injury.

Jack Sinclair is out of the game for St Kilda in the first half at Docklands against Western Bulldogs, after sustaining a calf injury.

  (Getty Images: AFL Photos/Michael Willson)

Aaron Naughton, Will Lewis and Rory Lobb all kicked two goals, with Lobb booting his goals at vital stages in the final quarter to see the Bulldogs home by 22 points, 12.11 (83) to 8.13 (61).

St Kilda had no multiple goalkickers, while Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera had 44 disposals, five inside 50s and gained 916 metres for his side.

The Saints slip out of the top 10 with the loss, while the Bulldogs lie seventh, outside the automatic finals spots only on percentage.

At the MCG, Cooper Trembath kicked a career-high four goals as the Kangaroos ran out winners over Richmond by 10.13 (73) to 6.12 (48).

Look back at how all the action unfolded in our live blog.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 6:26pm

By Andrew McGarry

That's all we have for round 15.

There were plenty of close ones and no blowouts for the round, and while the Kangaroos had things covered for most of the day at the MCG, the finale at Docklands was a lot more tense and in the balance.

Some great moments, including Marcus Bontempelli's goal, and a huge performance by Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera, were tempered by concerns for a number of players including St Kilda's Jack Sinclair and Tom De Koning. Their other big man Rowan Marshall went off with a shoulder issue, came back but could not finish the game.

So the loss will be doubly disappointing for the Saints, who slip out of the top 10 (replaced by the Kangaroos), while the Bulldogs are close to pushing their way into the top six.

We will be back on Thursday night for the start of round 16 with a ripsnorter of a clash at the Gabba between the Brisbane Lions and the Sydney Swans.

In the meantime, this is Andrew McGarry, thanking you for joining us today and wishing you a very good evening!

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 6:17pm

By Andrew McGarry

St Kilda's 22-point defeat to the Western Bulldogs at Docklands has been compounded by injuries to key duo Jack Sinclair and Tom De Koning.

Smashed in their last three outings against the Bulldogs, the Saints were forced to deal with adversity from the start on Sunday when Sinclair went down in the first quarter and De Koning in the second.

St Kilda battled on bravely and stayed in the contest until late but the Bulldogs' early buffer was enough as they secured a crucial win, 12.11 (83) to 8.13 (61).

St Kilda insisted Sinclair hurt his calf, but they would have serious concerns over an achilles injury after they put his foot in a moon boot when he hobbled from the field in pain.

An achilles rupture would rule the Saints co-captain out for the rest of the season, while a calf injury would mean far less time on the sidelines.

Highly-paid recruit De Koning produced a strong start but suffered a heavy hit to the ribs in the second quarter.

St Kilda's number one ruck was assessed in the rooms, before briefly returning to the field late in the second term.

But De Koning's condition worsened and he was ruled out of the match during the main break.

The Saints' other ruck, Rowan Marshall, bravely battled on after receiving treatment on a shoulder injury in the third quarter.

Star Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera was comfortably St Kilda's best, having 37 disposals to three-quarter-time and finishing with a career-best 44.

After a heavy loss to Adelaide last week, the Bulldogs responded in workmanlike fashion, with a clear focus on defence.

Against the Crows, the Bulldogs conceded nine first-quarter goals, but on Sunday they blunted St Kilda's attacking weapons while Buku Khamis and James O'Donnell held down the defensive 50.

Superstar captain Marcus Bontempelli (34 possessions and 13 clearances) was typically excellent, his classy goal late in the second quarter the highlight of a scrappy contest.

His willingness to take ruck contests to help Tim English early in the match was surprising, especially given he has dealt with soreness for most of the season.

The win lifts the Bulldogs to seventh (9-6), with a trip to the SCG to face premiership contenders Sydney to come following their bye next week.

St Kilda (6-9) also have a week off before meeting last-placed Essendon in round 17 as they face an uphill battle to qualify for the wildcard weekend.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:54pm

By Andrew McGarry

Late misses by Mitch Owens and Cooper Sharman and a goal from Ryan Byrnes completed the scoring, but the Saints have run out of puff and out of time.

They had chances in the final quarter, but whenever the Bulldogs were challenged they found the answer.

The Bulldogs win by 23 points, but the margin is irrelevant in the end.

They earn their ninth win of the season, and sit in seventh, out of the automatic finals spots on percentage.

St Kilda are in 12th after a tough, tough loss and they will be waiting for the injury report with trepidation.

Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera had 41 disposals, Hugo Garcia had 35, and Marcus Bontempelli had 34 plus THAT brilliant goal.

An entertaining and intense way to wrap up round 15!

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:48pm

By Andrew McGarry

The time is very late here, but the Saints are still coming.

They had an opening with Callum Wilkie getting the ball inside 50, but his curling kick just stayed out to the left.

That is definitely that.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:45pm

By Andrew McGarry

Andthere is the answer for the Bulldogs!

They get the centre clearance, go long to a contest, it comes off hands, Rhylee West handballs clear to Aaron Naughton, and the headbanded one snaps the vital goal to restore a 30-point margin.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:43pm

By Andrew McGarry

We're about to enter time on, and the Saints have managed to hit back. They've run it out of the back half, and got it inside 50 to Hugo Garcia, who steadies and kicks a great goal from the right forward pocket.

There is time, but can they do it? Four goals the gap.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:40pm

By Andrew McGarry

The swings of momentum are going minute to minute right now, and the Saints have got caught again.

They had it in forward 50 but it was cleared, and the Dogs went down the left wing. They had the numbers and there was always the extra man to take the handball or kick.

Finally there was the pass over the top to Rory Lobb in the square, and he hoisted it into the second deck from the goal-line.

The lead is out to 30 points and that must be close to it for the day.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:37pm

By Andrew McGarry

This is getting to a white heat here. Both sides are going for EVERYTHING. The Bulldogs smothered a kick from Nas on Saints D50, but couldn't turn it into a score.

The Saints broke downfield, and were trying to go inside 50 but they were chopped off.

We are closing on halfway in the final quarter, and right now the Bulldogs have this in control. But it would only take a goal or two to make the crowd decibel levels match a rocket liftoff.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:33pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Bulldogs sense an opening here, and they are trying to put the game away.

They kick long inside 50 to a pack (who are all standing), the ball lands in the arms of Rory Lobb!

Lobb goes back and kicks it, and the lead is now out to 25 points.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:29pm

By Andrew McGarry

Miss at one end, goal at the other!

The Bulldogs have it at half-back, then they switch it to the left wing before kicking stright to a mark, then a chip inside 50 to Artie Jones.

He marks and then kicks the goal, and the lead is out to 19 points!

The Saints need four unanswered goals, and it seems like they are putting Jack Silvagni up forward.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:27pm

By Andrew McGarry

This game is fast and furious already, and every chance is important.

The Saints go forward, and Mitch Owens lets loose a kick from inside 50 - but it hits the post! He celebrates as if a goal - but the umpire signals with one hand, not two.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:23pm

By Andrew McGarry

As we start the final term, there's no doubt who the key is for St Kilda.

Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera has, in three quarters of footy, had 37 disposals, kicked a goal and gained a crazy 867 metres.

Unless something happens, he seems likely to crack the 1,000m by the end of this. The Bulldogs need to try and find a way to stop him.

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:15pm

By Andrew McGarry

The siren sounds, and the Saints can't get the late goal they really want.

It's a 14-point game with a quarter to go.

The Bulldogs have lost their dominance, and the Saints are coming. But the injury toll is real, and could be a problem.

On the plus side for St Kilda, Rowan Marshall is back on the ground with his shoulder strapped. Can he see out the game?

They are going to be short of rotations as this match comes to a conclusion. Who will win? We're about to find out.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:07pm

By Andrew McGarry

We are in time on in the third quarter, and the Saints trail by 15 points.

So there is plenty of time left to turn this around, but they can't afford to miss opportunities.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:05pm

By Andrew McGarry

That could be a pivotal moment!

The Saints burst forward and Max Hall runs towards goal and kicks a great score.

But it won't count! He ran too far! The Saints fans are incensed, but that's a big moment. It could have been an eight-point lead, but the momentum is chopped off.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 5:00pm

By Andrew McGarry

Oh what a mistake from the Bulldogs!

That's an awful kickout from the Dogs, going across 50 and down the throat of young Saint Campbell Lake.

He marks inside 50, and kicks the goal!

That's a team lifter, and the margin is falling to 14 points.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:57pm

By Andrew McGarry

Are the Saints cursed today?

They've already lost two of their leading players, now Rowan Marshall has gone down after a contest, and he is holding his shoulder.

He gets up and waves the medics away, but a minute or two later he has come from the ground and gone down to the rooms.

Will pain relief keep him in the game? If it can't, then the Saints will be three players down. Unbelievable.

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:55pm

By Andrew McGarry

The Saints need something to start going right here, and they have one!

The ball went inside 50, the Saints kicked across 50 to a contest, but Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera was held as he tried to go for it.

The free followed and Nas kicked the goal! The lead is back to three goals, which is important.

We should also point out that Wanganeen-Milera is up to 32 disposals including 24 kicks, and we're barely a few minutes into the second half.

Key Event

Sun 21 Jun 2026 at 4:51pm

By Andrew McGarry

St Kilda is down to three rotations on the bench, as something changed during the half-time break with Tom De Koning's rib injury obviously causing him more grief.

He spoke briefly to Fox Footy coming off at half-time and sounded ok, but that's the end of his day, and that will make the Saints's task doubly hard now.
